TigreGotico/afrolid_1.5-onnx: unrecognised licence 'other' (not declared by the source repo, so sync_registry.py's licence gate blocks it before architecture is even considered) AND a separate, independent blocker even if licensed: it is an XLM-R sequence classifier over ~500 African language codes, and linguonnx.detect only implements the fastText-hash LID engine (GlotLIDFeaturizer + vocab.txt/labels.json/*_hash.py) - no tokenizer-based transformer classifier loader exists for it. Separately investigated for a suspected label-mapping defect: a genuine Yoruba sentence ('E ku aaro, oruko mi ni Joao, mo si ngbe ni Lisbon.') was classified Fula/Wolof at both precisions, yor absent from the top 5. Ruled out as our export or preprocessing: the exported config.json's id2label is byte-identical to UBC-NLP/afrolid_1.5's own config.json at every checked index (aar/aba/abn/.../ful=127/fuv=129/wol=490/yor=510), and running the unmodified upstream PyTorch checkpoint directly through transformers on the same sentence reproduces the identical Fula 0.39 / Wolof 0.27 / Tswana 0.23 misclassification with yor absent - confirmed genuine upstream model behaviour, not an export or preprocessing defect. Do not register until a transformer classifier engine exists; even then this specific input class needs a documented quality caveat.
TigreGotico/arabic-MARBERT-dialect-ident: unrecognised licence 'other' (not declared by the source repo, so sync_registry.py's licence gate blocks it before architecture is even considered) AND a separate, independent blocker even if licensed: it is a MARBERT (BERT-family) sequence classifier over Arabic *cities* (e.g. Cairo), not BCP-47 language tags, and linguonnx.detect only implements the fastText-hash LID engine (GlotLIDFeaturizer + vocab.txt/labels.json/*_hash.py) - no tokenizer-based transformer classifier loader exists, and lid.json's contract (BCP-47 out) would not fit a city label regardless. Hand-tested directly with transformers+onnxruntime outside this library: it correctly top-1s Cairo for Egyptian Arabic input at both fp32 and int8 - the model itself works, this library has no engine or registry section for it.
